subject: Physics
topic: Work, energy and power — mixed tiers
description: Definitions, units, KE/PE conversion, work-energy theorem, problem-solving

questions.stem: Work done by a constant force F over a displacement d in the same direction is given by:
questions.explanation: Work W = F · d cosθ (where θ = angle between force and displacement). When F is in same direction as d, θ = 0, cosθ = 1, so W = F × d. SI unit: joule (J) = newton·metre. If force is perpendicular to displacement (θ = 90°), W = 0 — e.g., gravity does NO work on a horizontally-moving object; centripetal force does NO work in circular motion.

questions.stem: Kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving at speed v is:
questions.explanation: Translational kinetic energy KE = ½mv² — joules in SI. m in kg, v in m/s. Doubling velocity QUADRUPLES the KE (a key safe-driving message). m·v is momentum (linear); m·v² is twice the KE; m·g·h is gravitational potential energy. Rotational KE = ½ I ω² (I — moment of inertia, ω — angular speed). Total KE for an object that translates AND rotates = sum of both.

questions.stem: Potential energy of a body of mass 5 kg raised to a height of 10 m above ground (g = 10 m/s²) is:
questions.explanation: Gravitational PE = m·g·h = 5 × 10 × 10 = 500 J. Sign convention — usually positive if h measured up from a reference; can be negative if below reference. Alternative — elastic PE = ½kx² for a spring stretched by x. Conservation of mechanical energy: KE + PE = constant (in absence of friction). Free-fall: PE→KE conversion. At a pendulum's lowest point, PE→0, KE max; at extremes, KE→0, PE max.

options.option_text: Rate of doing work; energy per unit time (P = W/t)

questions.explanation: Power P = W/t = energy/time. SI unit: watt (W) = J/s. 1 horsepower (hp) = 746 W ≈ 0.75 kW. Bulb rated 60 W consumes 60 J/s. 1 kWh (kilowatt-hour) = 3.6 × 10⁶ J = 1 unit of electricity (the billing unit). For circuits: P = V·I = I²·R = V²/R. The car horsepower is a good intuitive comparator — a 100-hp car can do 100×746 J = 74.6 kJ of work per second.

questions.stem: A pump delivers 1500 J of energy in 5 seconds. Its power output is:
questions.explanation: P = W/t = 1500 / 5 = 300 W. Power = energy delivered per second. Compare household appliances: tube light ~40 W, ceiling fan ~70 W, fridge ~200 W (steady state), microwave ~800 W, AC ~1500 W (per ton).

questions.stem: By the work-energy theorem, the net work done on a moving object equals:
questions.explanation: Work-Energy Theorem: W_net = ΔKE = ½m(v² − u²), where u and v are initial and final speeds. Positive work → KE increases (object accelerates); negative work (e.g., friction, brakes) → KE decreases. Foundational to all energy problems in mechanics. Implies if you know force × distance, you can find final velocity without doing kinematics. Doesn't depend on path — only initial / final states (path-independence is true for conservative forces only).

questions.stem: A 100 W bulb operating for 10 hours consumes electrical energy equal to:
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 100 W × 10 h = 1,000 Wh = 1 kWh = 1 'unit' on your electricity bill. At ₹6/unit (typical residential), that costs ₹6. LED bulb of equivalent brightness consumes ~10 W → 90% energy saving. India's CFL/LED rollout (UJALA scheme since 2015) has saved billions of kWh.
